touches.text: The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a design agent comes after that. Until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.

The workflow drives it. When a step's work is finished, the ticket asks that step's gate. Once the gate passes, its post-gate probes send mail over the bus to every device that can do the next step, naming the step (BUILDME, PROVEME, ...), and a device comes to claim it. A builder never goes looking for what's next: it gets the mail and does that. When several compete, the least capable one that thinks it can do it claims it, leaving the more capable free for bigger work.
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
They live inside the Recovery device (6.3.4), since recovery has to work when other things don't.

A trouble ticket is a work order. Whoever fixed it reports the fix to the originator (the device or machine that raised it), and the originator marks it fixed. A trouble that comes back is not designed for yet; if recurrent problems appear, we'll explore that.
Transient: things held for seconds to days (mail, logs, test runs, trouble tickets, inference tickets). The logging tree.

Cairn owns all of ~/.cairn/ and delegates each ~/.cairn/devices/ subtree to its device. Everything outside devices/ (~/.cairn/logging/ and the rest) is Cairn's, so every log is Cairn's and Cairn cleans them up in sleep. Transient things are files there; trouble tickets are logging items.
Cairn's own sleep has a lot to do, including clearing the logging tree of things older than 30 days (4.3.2).
Trouble tickets (3.4.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.3.7.1.3).

Its web panel is the operator's to-do list: email, trouble tickets, open questions (the ones only the operator can answer). The list is live: items appear as they arrive and leave as they're answered or resolved.
